chunks: A Jew passed by the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Al-Sam be upon you.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Upon you.' His companions said, 'But he greeted you with death!' He (the Prophet) said, 'Death be upon you' — then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'And that is how I replied.'

Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This Jew will be bitten by a black snake in the nape of his neck, and it will kill him.' So the Jew went and gathered a lot of firewood and carried it. Then, before long, he came back. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Put it down.' He placed the firewood down, and behold — a black snake was in the middle of the firewood, biting on a stick.

So he said: 'O Jew! What did you do today?' He said, 'I did not do anything except carry this firewood of mine. I came back with it, and I had two cakes with me; I ate one and gave the other in charity to a poor person.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'By it God repelled it from him.' And he said: 'Indeed, charity repels an evil death from the human being.'

key_terms.السَّامُ: A play on the Arabic/Hebrew word for 'death' or 'poison'; the Jew intended a curse disguised as a greeting
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةَ: Sadaqa — voluntary charity; here it is the direct cause of divine protection
key_terms.مِيتَةَ السَّوْءِ: Evil death — an unnatural, harmful, or sudden death considered inauspicious

ai.seo_question: Does charity protect from evil death in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a story of the Prophet (SAWW) and a Jewish man who unknowingly saved himself from a fatal snakebite through a single act of charity. The Prophet foresaw the man's death by snakebite, but when the Jew confessed to giving one of his two cakes to a poor person, the Prophet revealed that this small act of charity had warded off the deadly fate. The hadith concludes with a universal principle: charity repels evil death from a person, illustrating the spiritual and protective power of generosity.
